label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday at Embakasi: casuals' pay (for Brian)

Brian,

The short version: the money goes to their phones by M-Pesa by 11am Monday, in full, plus KES 500 each on top. That is two hours after the Kisumu trucks have to leave, so you will be asking them to load on our word. Everything below is about making that word one we can keep.

**What happened on Friday**

This was our mistake and the guys did nothing wrong. Please go in on that footing, not defending us.

- Mlimani Bank upgraded their payment platform on 25 November and now require a new file template.
- Our file for the 212 casuals went up on Friday in the old format and the bank rejected the whole thing just before 2pm. Not one payment went through.
- The rejection notice went to an old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, and by then the bank's cut-off had passed.
- Kevin has said plainly that this one is on finance.

When you tell the guys, tell it as the company's error. Don't lean on the bank's upgrade. We missed the alert, and they will hear the difference.

**When the money lands**

- We are skipping the bank and paying everyone by M-Pesa. Njeri approved it on Saturday morning.
- Kevin's commitment is money on phones by 11am Monday. He will not promise earlier, so neither do we.
- That is before rent falls due on the 1st, which is what many of them are worried about.
- Peninah has confirmed 198 of the 212 numbers. The other 14 she could not reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake.
- She will be at the depot from 7:30 with the printed list so those 14 can give her correct numbers face to face. She is also bringing the laptop for anyone who wants a payslip printed.

**What you can promise**

- Full pay by M-Pesa by 11am Monday for everyone whose number is confirmed.
- KES 500 per head for Monday's lunch and fare, for every casual on the affected list, in the same payment.
- No M-Pesa charges deducted from anyone. The company carries them.
- Peninah on site from 7:30 with the list, for wrong numbers and payslips.
- An apology from management, in person. Njeri asked for it specifically and asked that you give it. Say it first, before anything about trucks.
- Anyone whose amount looks wrong once it lands goes to Peninah on the spot, or through Joseph and then to HR within 48 hours, as the procedure says.

**What you mustn't**

- Any time earlier than 11. Not "this morning", not "before you finish loading", not "any minute now". In Mombasa in 2024 a supervisor told the casuals "by lunch", the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. Joseph tells me our own guys are already saying that last time management said "tomorrow" for three days. If someone asks whether it could come earlier, the answer is "by 11, and I'm not going to give you a time I can't keep".
- The 11am time to the 14 until Peninah or Kevin confirms they are in the same run. Until then their line is: see Peninah at 7:30, give her your number, and she will tell you when.
- Anything extra to get the trucks loaded. The 500 is what Njeri approved. No bonus and no deal on the side.
- A new time if 11 passes and the money has not landed. Call Kevin, tell the guys exactly what he tells you, and nothing more.
- Anything at all about contracts, in either direction. See the next section.

**If Ouma's group won't load**

Joseph says Ouma and two others are telling people not to load the Kisumu trucks until they see money. Ouma is loud but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent to pay, and he is frightened more than he is making trouble.

In order:

1. Get the mood from Joseph when you arrive at 5:30. He has been trying to calm them since Saturday.
2. Talk to Ouma first, privately, before you speak to the group. Tell him what you will tell everyone: what went wrong, 11am, the 500, Peninah at 7:30. Let him ask what he wants. If he hears it from you man to man, he may well carry it to the others himself.
3. Then the whole group: the apology, what happened, the time. Be straight that you are asking them to load before the money arrives and that you know what you are asking, given Friday.
4. Point them to Peninah at 7:30. Someone from payroll standing there with the list will do more than anything either of us can say.

If some still refuse, the procedure (v3 in this folder) is clear on two things. A stoppage is handled by Ops and HR together. And nobody is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. So no talk of contracts, of who gets called for the next shift, or of names being taken.

The difficulty is that I am in the air from 7:05 until about 8:30, which is exactly when this would be happening. So let us agree the line now, and treat this document as our joint decision for that window:

- Those who are willing to load, load. Nobody leans on those who are not.
- Those who refuse wait at the depot for their money like everyone else. Nothing is said to them about consequences.
- No new promises to get the trucks out by 9.
- Anything beyond this that touches the men waits until you and I have spoken.

How you cover the trucks and the mill's offloading slot is your call, and you know your options better than I do. You should know by about 8 whether 9 is still possible.

If you disagree with any of this, tell me on Sunday so we change it together before Monday.

**Reaching me**

- I am up from 4:30. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes: Kevin's timing, the mood on the ground, anything from Joseph overnight.
- I should have my phone back on by about 8:30.
- Kevin for anything about the payment itself.
- Peninah for the list and the 14.

Achieng
